text.p: British Airways Plc said on Wednesday it would be looking for around 5,000 staff to take voluntary severance or early retirement over the next 18 months.
But the airline will also seek to recruit a similar number of staff -- with different skills -- over the next three years.

The announcement formed part of British Airways' ambitious "Step Change" efficiency drive aimed at cutting a further one billion stg from its annual cost base before 2000. The airline said it expects to employ around the same number of people in 2000, but the skill composition of its 49,000-strong UK workforce was expected to be different.

"I do not expect wholesale job losses," said chief executive Robert Ayling. "Jobs will also be created, and jobs secured. We will grow and we will improve. I am committed to a strategy of investment and improved profitability."

Ayling announced earlier this year he intended to find efficiency improvements which would cut the airline's annual cost base by one billion stg within the next three years to offset continuing falls in average fare levels and the rising costs of handling more traffic.

Ayling said on Wednesday: "Today marks the start of the next stage on our long journey from privatisation. For neasrly 10 years we have competed successfully and flourished as a private company...but the market in which we are operating is changing rapidly."

"The competition is getting better and more efficient. Our customers expect more but our cost of providing a seat has risen faster than the price customers pay in a highly-competitive marketplace," he said.

The airline said management and staff would would work together to identify areas throughout the company where revenues can be increased, utilisation of assets can be improved or costs can be reduced to get the one billion stg of savings targeted.

"Some activities could be sold or subcontracted if they can be done better or more cheaply externally, with employees involved being offered jobs with the new owner, redeployed withing the airline with retraining, or taking voluntary severance or early retirement," the airline said in a statement.

"In the coming months we will unveil new product, brand and customer service plans. We will confirm our investment plans for new aircraft worth hundreds of millions of pounds, and for new sales and customer service technology," the company said.

Earlier this year, Ayling said management was looking at areas where it might consider buying in services if they were cheaper than in-house operations, and was looking at "all the ancillary services that go to make up the day-to-day operations of an airline, of which there are huge numbers".

"We will be making sure that wherever possible services provided within the company are at competitive rates...If that can't be achieved then we will buy in the services rather than provide them from within the company," he said then. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
